title: Qian Chibi Fu / Hou Chibi Fu (Rhapsody on the Red Cliffs, First and Second)

access.edition_or_version: Burton Watson, Su Tung-p'o: Selections from a Sung Dynasty Poet (Columbia University Press, 1965) — verified English anchor. Original classical Chinese text public domain; translation copyrighted.

tone_mechanisms_observed: reflection staged as guest-question / host-answer dialogue so it never becomes soliloquy
place-names and the dated occasion (Huangzhou exile, 1082) fix the meditation in an actual site and circumstance
question-form philosophical lexis: the reflective turn proceeds by interrogative exchange rather than declaration
the scale pivot — small self against vast time — as the celebrated self-distancing move
mechanics.point_of_view: Two voices: a guest voices the problem of impermanence; the host answers by re-deriving the vantage point (river and moon as enduring, the human moment as borrowed).
mechanics.tense_and_structure: Present-at-the-site scenic description opening into historical past (Three Kingdoms allusion) and back — temporal layering comparable to Wordsworth's stacked tenses (dossier §E comparative note).
mechanics.rhythm_and_cadence: Parallelism and tonal cadence typical of fu slow the pace at the reflective turn; scenic momentum yields to measured questioning.
mechanics.psychic_distance: Distance is opened by scale comparison, not psychological jargon — a cross-cultural instance of self-distancing (supports clm-tone-reflective-self-distanced-reflection by analogy).
mechanics.style_and_devices: The river/moon figure carries the philosophical work so narration need not state a thesis; the paired fu structure (first dialogue, second more analytic) institutionalizes the reflective pivot.
mechanics.copyright_note: Original classical Chinese text public domain; Watson translation copyrighted. Described by technique only; no passage reproduced.
mechanics.translation_note: The fu's question-answer architecture and tonal parallelism are only partly recoverable in English; pin Watson page numbers before quoting the translation.
